325|    static func boundsForPoints(_ points: [NSPoint], padding: CGFloat) -> NSRect? {
326|        guard let first = points.first else { return nil }
327|        var minX = first.x
328|        var minY = first.y
329|        var maxX = first.x
330|        var maxY = first.y
331|        for point in points.dropFirst() {
332|            minX = min(minX, point.x)
333|            minY = min(minY, point.y)
334|            maxX = max(maxX, point.x)
335|            maxY = max(maxY, point.y)
336|        }
337|        return NSRect(x: minX - padding,
338|                      y: minY - padding,
339|                      width: (maxX - minX) + (padding * 2),
340|                      height: (maxY - minY) + (padding * 2))
341|    }

357|    /// by arrow drawing, bounds, and hit-testing so they never disagree.
358|    static func arrowHeadPoints(from start: NSPoint, to end: NSPoint) -> (NSPoint, NSPoint) {
359|        let dx = end.x - start.x
360|        let dy = end.y - start.y
361|        let angle = atan2(dy, dx)
362|        let point1 = NSPoint(x: end.x - arrowHeadLength * cos(angle - arrowHeadAngle),
363|                             y: end.y - arrowHeadLength * sin(angle - arrowHeadAngle))
364|        let point2 = NSPoint(x: end.x - arrowHeadLength * cos(angle + arrowHeadAngle),
365|                             y: end.y - arrowHeadLength * sin(angle + arrowHeadAngle))
366|        return (point1, point2)

  1|# Zoomies
  2|
  3|_Take and copy paste screen in 2 seconds. Rename? 3 seconds. Rename + annotate with prompt for agent? 5 seconds. Quick edit? 7? maybe 10..._
  4|
  5|> **Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.** If you have an older macOS version, it is probably best to use this as a product spec and build your own. I had enough headaches with older OS versions already.
  6|>
  7|> Zoomies builds natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Intel is supported but untested because I do not have an Intel Mac.
  8|
  9|Mac-only keyboard-first screenshot and scratchpad app for agentic coding.
 10|Good for touchpad users too, especially if your wrist is already cooked from gaming.
 11|
 12|Fork it, pork it, change it, rebuild it. Have fun.
 13|
 14|## What It Does
 15|
 16|- Captures the exact UI state you want a coding agent to understand.
 17|- Adds quick notes/prompts to screenshots so the context travels with the image.
 18|- Saves Zoomies edit data inside PNGs, so future reopens can edit/delete Zoomies-added arrows, text, pen strokes, shapes, pasted selections, and cut regions.
 19|- Creates quick scratchpad notes for errors, issues, and ideas you spot in one project while your head is still in another.
 20|- Lets you rename, annotate, save, copy, or delete without breaking coding flow.
 21|- Reopens a selected Finder image and sends it back through the Zoomies flow.
 22|
 23|When you edit and save a non-PNG image such as a JPEG or HEIC, Zoomies saves the
 24|edited result as a PNG and removes the original non-PNG file.
 25|
 26|## Quick Start
 27|
 28|```bash
 29|cd zoomies
 30|swift build
 31|swift run Zoomies
 32|```
 33|
 34|To build a clickable `.app`:
 35|
 36|```bash
 37|./scripts/build_app.sh
 38|open dist/Zoomies.app
 39|```
 40|
 41|A coding agent can run that build script for you too.
 42|
 43|### Building on an Intel Mac
 44|
 45|Intel users should build Zoomies from source on their Intel Mac:
 46|
 47|```bash
 48|git clone https://github.com/bald-ai/zoomies.git
 49|cd zoomies
 50|./scripts/build_app.sh
 51|open dist/Zoomies.app
 52|```
 53|
 54|Swift automatically builds for the Mac it is running on: Apple silicon produces
 55|an `arm64` app, while Intel produces an `x86_64` app. A universal binary is only
 56|needed when distributing one prebuilt `.app` for both architectures; this
 57|repository distributes source instead.
 58|
 59|Intel support requires an Intel Mac running macOS 14 or later with Xcode 15 or
 60|later. **I do not own an Intel Mac, so the Intel build has not been personally
 61|tested.**
 62|
 63|## Default Shortcuts
 64|
 65|- `Option+Shift+4` -> area capture
 66|- `Option+Shift+3` -> full-screen capture
 67|- `Option+Shift+2` -> select an image in Finder, press this to edit/rename it with Zoomies
 68|- `Option+Shift+1` -> create a scratchpad note
 69|- `Option+Shift+5` -> start/stop screen recording (requires macOS 15)
 70|
 71|The defaults intentionally avoid the standard macOS `Cmd+Shift` screenshot shortcuts.
 72|
 73|You can change the main global shortcuts in Zoomies Settings. If you want to
 74|change keybinds that are not exposed in the UI, ask your coding agent to update
 75|the relevant shortcut code and build a new `.app` for you.
 76|
 77|## Workflow Keybinds
 78|
 79|| Screen | Key | Action |
 80|| --- | --- | --- |
 81|| Rename / Prompt | `Enter` | Save |
 82|| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
 83|| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Backspace` | Copy + delete |
 84|| Rename / Prompt | `Esc` | Delete / close |
 85|| Flow | `Tab` | Next step |
 86|| Flow | `Shift+Tab` | Previous step |
 87|| Edit | `W` / `A` / `R` / `E` / `T` / `S` | Pen / arrow / rectangle / ellipse / text / select |
 88|| Edit | `K` or `Q` | Open colors |
 89|| Edit | `1-6` | Pick color |
 90|| Edit | `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` | Undo / redo |
 91|| Edit | `Option+Backspace` | Clear |
 92|| Edit | `Cmd+C` / `Cmd+X` / `Cmd+V` | Copy / cut / paste |
 93|| Edit | `Cmd +` / `Cmd -` / `Cmd 0` | Zoom in / out / reset |
 94|| Edit | `Enter` | Save |
 95|| Edit | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
 96|| Edit | `Esc` | Cancel |
 97|
 98|## Editor Select Tool
 99|
100|Press `S` in the editor to use Select.
101|
102|Select now has two jobs:
103|
104|- Click a Zoomies-added object, like text, arrow, pen stroke, rectangle, ellipse, pasted image, or cut/erase region, to select it.
105|- Drag the selected object to move it, or press `Delete` to remove it.
106|- Drag on empty screenshot space to select a rectangular image region.
107|- With a region selected, use `Cmd+C` to copy it, `Cmd+X` to cut it, and `Cmd+V` to paste it back into the canvas.
108|- Switching to another tool clears the rectangular area selection.
109|
110|Select does not change the contents or shape of an existing annotation. To edit
111|existing text, press `T` for the Text tool and double-click the text. Arrows,
112|pen strokes, rectangles, and ellipses can be moved or deleted, but not reshaped.
113|
114|Editable objects are remembered only for PNGs saved by this version of Zoomies or later. Older already-flattened screenshots still open as normal images because their arrows/text are already baked into the pixels.
115|
116|## Screen Recording
117|
118|`Option+Shift+5` or the menu-bar icon's Start Recording begins a display
119|recording. There is no display picker: recording starts on the display under
120|the pointer and follows the pointer to another monitor after it stays there
121|for half a second. It keeps recording across app and Space changes, includes
122|the cursor, excludes Zoomies' own windows, and stops automatically after 60
123|seconds.
124|
125|Video is 30, 60, or 120 fps (selectable in Settings, default 30), SDR, H.264 MP4 without audio on a fixed 1920x1080 canvas
126|(the full display is fitted without cropping or stretching, with black
127|margins where needed). The menu bar shows only the elapsed seconds, from `0` to `60`, in red. The finished video is saved beside screenshots with a unique
128|`Recording_...` filename and revealed in Finder.
129|
130|Only one Zoomies operation runs at a time: recording blocks
131|screenshots/notes/Finder-reopen, and those workflows block recording startup.
132|Screen recording requires macOS 15 or later; on macOS 14 the menu command
133|explains it is unavailable while screenshots and notes keep working.
134|
135|## Temporary Clipboard Files
136|
137|`Copy + Delete` needs a temporary file so macOS can still paste the screenshot
138|after Zoomies removes it from the Desktop. Zoomies stores that temporary copy in
139|`~/Library/Caches/zoomies/clipboard` and clears the folder the next time Zoomies
140|starts.
141|
142|## Permissions
143|
144|Area capture uses the built-in macOS screenshot selector. Full-screen capture uses `ScreenCaptureKit` (`SCScreenshotManager`). macOS will prompt for Screen Recording permission when needed.
145|
146|For area capture, drag to select, press Space to switch to window/menu selection, or press Escape to cancel. The captured image then opens in the usual Zoomies workflow.
147|
148|- **Screen Recording** (for screenshots via ScreenCaptureKit)
149|- **Automation / Finder** (for reopening flow on selected Finder image via `Option+Shift+2`)
150|
151|### Permission after rebuilding the app
152|
153|If you edit the code and build a new copy of Zoomies, macOS may ask for
154|permission again even though Zoomies still appears to be allowed in System
155|Settings. The listed permission can belong to the previous app build.
156|
157|Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the relevant permission,
158|use the **−** button to remove the old Zoomies entry, then use the **+** button
159|to add and allow the newly built `Zoomies.app`.
</file-view>

content.oldText:
# Zoomies

_Take and copy paste screen in 2 seconds. Rename? 3 seconds. Rename + annotate with prompt for agent? 5 seconds. Quick edit? 7? maybe 10..._

> **Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.** If you have an older macOS version, it is probably best to use this as a product spec and build your own. I had enough headaches with older OS versions already.
>
> Zoomies builds natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Intel is supported but untested because I do not have an Intel Mac.

Mac-only keyboard-first screenshot and scratchpad app for agentic coding.
Good for touchpad users too, especially if your wrist is already cooked from gaming.

Fork it, pork it, change it, rebuild it. Have fun.

## What It Does

- Captures the exact UI state you want a coding agent to understand.
- Adds quick notes/prompts to screenshots so the context travels with the image.
- Saves Zoomies edit data inside PNGs, so future reopens can edit/delete Zoomies-added arrows, text, pen strokes, shapes, pasted selections, and cut regions.
- Creates quick scratchpad notes for errors, issues, and ideas you spot in one project while your head is still in another.
- Lets you rename, annotate, save, copy, or delete without breaking coding flow.
- Reopens a selected Finder image and sends it back through the Zoomies flow.

When you edit and save a non-PNG image such as a JPEG or HEIC, Zoomies saves the
edited result as a PNG and removes the original non-PNG file.

## Quick Start

```bash
cd zoomies
swift build
swift run Zoomies
```

To build a clickable `.app`:

```bash
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

A coding agent can run that build script for you too.

### Building on an Intel Mac

Intel users should build Zoomies from source on their Intel Mac:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bald-ai/zoomies.git
cd zoomies
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

Swift automatically builds for the Mac it is running on: Apple silicon produces
an `arm64` app, while Intel produces an `x86_64` app. A universal binary is only
needed when distributing one prebuilt `.app` for both architectures; this
repository distributes source instead.

Intel support requires an Intel Mac running macOS 14 or later with Xcode 15 or
later. **I do not own an Intel Mac, so the Intel build has not been personally
tested.**

## Default Shortcuts

- `Option+Shift+4` -> area capture
- `Option+Shift+3` -> full-screen capture
- `Option+Shift+2` -> select an image in Finder, press this to edit/rename it with Zoomies
- `Option+Shift+1` -> create a scratchpad note
- `Option+Shift+5` -> start/stop screen recording (requires macOS 15)

The defaults intentionally avoid the standard macOS `Cmd+Shift` screenshot shortcuts.

You can change the main global shortcuts in Zoomies Settings. If you want to
change keybinds that are not exposed in the UI, ask your coding agent to update
the relevant shortcut code and build a new `.app` for you.

## Workflow Keybinds

| Screen | Key | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rename / Prompt | `Enter` | Save |
| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Backspace` | Copy + delete |
| Rename / Prompt | `Esc` | Delete / close |
| Flow | `Tab` | Next step |
| Flow | `Shift+Tab` | Previous step |
| Edit | `W` / `A` / `R` / `E` / `T` / `S` | Pen / arrow / rectangle / ellipse / text / select |
| Edit | `K` or `Q` | Open colors |
| Edit | `1-6` | Pick color |
| Edit | `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` | Undo / redo |
| Edit | `Option+Backspace` | Clear |
| Edit | `Cmd+C` / `Cmd+X` / `Cmd+V` | Copy / cut / paste |
| Edit | `Cmd +` / `Cmd -` / `Cmd 0` | Zoom in / out / reset |
| Edit | `Enter` | Save |
| Edit | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
| Edit | `Esc` | Cancel |

## Editor Select Tool

Press `S` in the editor to use Select.

Select now has two jobs:

- Click a Zoomies-added object, like text, arrow, pen stroke, rectangle, ellipse, pasted image, or cut/erase region, to select it.
- Drag the selected object to move it, or press `Delete` to remove it.
- Drag on empty screenshot space to select a rectangular image region.
- With a region selected, use `Cmd+C` to copy it, `Cmd+X` to cut it, and `Cmd+V` to paste it back into the canvas.
- Switching to another tool clears the rectangular area selection.

Select does not change the contents or shape of an existing annotation. To edit
existing text, press `T` for the Text tool and double-click the text. Arrows,
pen strokes, rectangles, and ellipses can be moved or deleted, but not reshaped.

Editable objects are remembered only for PNGs saved by this version of Zoomies or later. Older already-flattened screenshots still open as normal images because their arrows/text are already baked into the pixels.

## Screen Recording

`Option+Shift+5` or the menu-bar icon's Start Recording begins a display
recording. There is no display picker: recording starts on the display under
the pointer and follows the pointer to another monitor after it stays there
for half a second. It keeps recording across app and Space changes, includes
the cursor, excludes Zoomies' own windows, and stops automatically after 60
seconds.

Video is 30, 60, or 120 fps (selectable in Settings, default 30), SDR, H.264 MP4 without audio on a fixed 1920x1080 canvas
(the full display is fitted without cropping or stretching, with black
margins where needed). The menu bar shows only the elapsed seconds, from `0` to `60`, in red. The finished video is saved beside screenshots with a unique
`Recording_...` filename and revealed in Finder.

Only one Zoomies operation runs at a time: recording blocks
screenshots/notes/Finder-reopen, and those workflows block recording startup.
Screen recording requires macOS 15 or later; on macOS 14 the menu command
explains it is unavailable while screenshots and notes keep working.

## Temporary Clipboard Files

`Copy + Delete` needs a temporary file so macOS can still paste the screenshot
after Zoomies removes it from the Desktop. Zoomies stores that temporary copy in
`~/Library/Caches/zoomies/clipboard` and clears the folder the next time Zoomies
starts.

## Permissions

Area capture uses the built-in macOS screenshot selector. Full-screen capture uses `ScreenCaptureKit` (`SCScreenshotManager`). macOS will prompt for Screen Recording permission when needed.

For area capture, drag to select, press Space to switch to window/menu selection, or press Escape to cancel. The captured image then opens in the usual Zoomies workflow.

- **Screen Recording** (for screenshots via ScreenCaptureKit)
- **Automation / Finder** (for reopening flow on selected Finder image via `Option+Shift+2`)

### Permission after rebuilding the app

If you edit the code and build a new copy of Zoomies, macOS may ask for
permission again even though Zoomies still appears to be allowed in System
Settings. The listed permission can belong to the previous app build.

Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the relevant permission,
use the **−** button to remove the old Zoomies entry, then use the **+** button
to add and allow the newly built `Zoomies.app`.

# Zoomies

_Take and copy paste screen in 2 seconds. Rename? 3 seconds. Rename + annotate with prompt for agent? 5 seconds. Quick edit? 7? maybe 10..._

> **Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.** If you have an older macOS version, it is probably best to use this as a product spec and build your own. I had enough headaches with older OS versions already.
>
> Zoomies builds natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Intel is supported but untested because I do not have an Intel Mac.

Mac-only keyboard-first screenshot and scratchpad app for agentic coding.
Good for touchpad users too, especially if your wrist is already cooked from gaming.

Fork it, pork it, change it, rebuild it. Have fun.

## What It Does

- Captures the exact UI state you want a coding agent to understand.
- Adds quick notes/prompts to screenshots so the context travels with the image.
- Saves Zoomies edit data inside PNGs, so future reopens can edit/delete Zoomies-added arrows, text, pen strokes, shapes, pasted selections, and cut regions.
- Creates quick scratchpad notes for errors, issues, and ideas you spot in one project while your head is still in another.
- Lets you rename, annotate, save, copy, or delete without breaking coding flow.
- Reopens a selected Finder image and sends it back through the Zoomies flow.

When you edit and save a non-PNG image such as a JPEG or HEIC, Zoomies saves the
edited result as a PNG and removes the original non-PNG file.

## Quick Start

```bash
cd zoomies
swift build
swift run Zoomies
```

To build a clickable `.app`:

```bash
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

A coding agent can run that build script for you too.

### Building on an Intel Mac

Intel users should build Zoomies from source on their Intel Mac:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bald-ai/zoomies.git
cd zoomies
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

Swift automatically builds for the Mac it is running on: Apple silicon produces
an `arm64` app, while Intel produces an `x86_64` app. A universal binary is only
needed when distributing one prebuilt `.app` for both architectures; this
repository distributes source instead.

Intel support requires an Intel Mac running macOS 14 or later with Xcode 15 or
later. **I do not own an Intel Mac, so the Intel build has not been personally
tested.**

## Default Shortcuts

- `Option+Shift+4` -> area capture
- `Option+Shift+3` -> full-screen capture
- `Option+Shift+2` -> select an image in Finder, press this to edit/rename it with Zoomies
- `Option+Shift+1` -> create a scratchpad note
- `Option+Shift+5` -> start/stop screen recording (requires macOS 15)

The defaults intentionally avoid the standard macOS `Cmd+Shift` screenshot shortcuts.

You can change the main global shortcuts in Zoomies Settings. If you want to
change keybinds that are not exposed in the UI, ask your coding agent to update
the relevant shortcut code and build a new `.app` for you.

## Workflow Keybinds

| Screen | Key | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rename / Prompt | `Enter` | Save |
| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Backspace` | Copy + delete |
| Rename / Prompt | `Esc` | Delete / close |
| Flow | `Tab` | Next step |
| Flow | `Shift+Tab` | Previous step |
| Edit | `W` / `D` / `A` / `R` / `E` / `T` / `F` / `S` | Pen / line / arrow / rectangle / ellipse / text / numbered marker / select |
| Edit | `K` or `Q` | Open colors |
| Edit | `1-6` | Pick color |
| Edit | `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` | Undo / redo |
| Edit | `Option+Backspace` | Clear |
| Edit | `Cmd+C` / `Cmd+X` / `Cmd+V` | Copy / cut / paste |
| Edit | `Cmd +` / `Cmd -` / `Cmd 0` | Zoom in / out / reset |
| Edit | `Enter` | Save |
| Edit | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
| Edit | `Esc` | Cancel |

## Editor Select Tool

Press `S` in the editor to use Select.

Select now has two jobs:

- Click a Zoomies-added object, like text, arrow, pen stroke, rectangle, ellipse, pasted image, or cut/erase region, to select it.
- Drag the selected object to move it, or press `Delete` to remove it.
- Drag on empty screenshot space to select a rectangular image region.
- With a region selected, use `Cmd+C` to copy it, `Cmd+X` to cut it, and `Cmd+V` to paste it back into the canvas.
- Switching to another tool clears the rectangular area selection.

Select does not change the contents or shape of an existing annotation. To edit
existing text, press `T` for the Text tool and double-click the text. Arrows,
pen strokes, rectangles, and ellipses can be moved or deleted, but not reshaped.

Editable objects are remembered only for PNGs saved by this version of Zoomies or later. Older already-flattened screenshots still open as normal images because their arrows/text are already baked into the pixels.

## Screen Recording

`Option+Shift+5` or the menu-bar icon's Start Recording begins a display
recording. There is no display picker: recording starts on the display under
the pointer and follows the pointer to another monitor after it stays there
for half a second. It keeps recording across app and Space changes, includes
the cursor, excludes Zoomies' own windows, and stops automatically after 60
seconds.

Video is 30, 60, or 120 fps (selectable in Settings, default 30), SDR, H.264 MP4 without audio on a fixed 1920x1080 canvas
(the full display is fitted without cropping or stretching, with black
margins where needed). The menu bar shows only the elapsed seconds, from `0` to `60`, in red. The finished video is saved beside screenshots with a unique
`Recording_...` filename and revealed in Finder.

Only one Zoomies operation runs at a time: recording blocks
screenshots/notes/Finder-reopen, and those workflows block recording startup.
Screen recording requires macOS 15 or later; on macOS 14 the menu command
explains it is unavailable while screenshots and notes keep working.

## Temporary Clipboard Files

`Copy + Delete` needs a temporary file so macOS can still paste the screenshot
after Zoomies removes it from the Desktop. Zoomies stores that temporary copy in
`~/Library/Caches/zoomies/clipboard` and clears the folder the next time Zoomies
starts.

## Permissions

Area capture uses the built-in macOS screenshot selector. Full-screen capture uses `ScreenCaptureKit` (`SCScreenshotManager`). macOS will prompt for Screen Recording permission when needed.

For area capture, drag to select, press Space to switch to window/menu selection, or press Escape to cancel. The captured image then opens in the usual Zoomies workflow.

- **Screen Recording** (for screenshots via ScreenCaptureKit)
- **Automation / Finder** (for reopening flow on selected Finder image via `Option+Shift+2`)

### Permission after rebuilding the app

If you edit the code and build a new copy of Zoomies, macOS may ask for
permission again even though Zoomies still appears to be allowed in System
Settings. The listed permission can belong to the previous app build.

Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the relevant permission,
use the **−** button to remove the old Zoomies entry, then use the **+** button
to add and allow the newly built `Zoomies.app`.

args.old_string:
## Editor Select Tool

Press `S` in the editor to use Select.

Select now has two jobs:

- Click a Zoomies-added object, like text, arrow, pen stroke, rectangle, ellipse, pasted image, or cut/erase region, to select it.
- Drag the selected object to move it, or press `Delete` to remove it.
- Drag on empty screenshot space to select a rectangular image region.
- With a region selected, use `Cmd+C` to copy it, `Cmd+X` to cut it, and `Cmd+V` to paste it back into the canvas.
- Switching to another tool clears the rectangular area selection.

Select does not change the contents or shape of an existing annotation. To edit
existing text, press `T` for the Text tool and double-click the text. Arrows,
pen strokes, rectangles, and ellipses can be moved or deleted, but not reshaped.
args.new_string:
## Editor Numbered Markers

Press `F` in the editor to use the numbered marker tool.

- Click on the image to stamp a filled circle labeled `1`, then `2`, `3`, and so on, in the current annotation color. Markers stay readable on light and dark images, and the circle widens instead of clipping for multi-digit numbers.
- Drag an existing marker to move it, double-click it to retype its number, or press `Delete` to remove it. Removing a marker never renumbers the others, and the next number continues past the highest existing marker.
- Reference the numbers in your note text — the note is saved below the image, so prompts like "fix 1 and 3" travel with the screenshot.

## Editor Select Tool

Press `S` in the editor to use Select.

Select now has two jobs:

- Click a Zoomies-added object, like text, numbered marker, arrow, pen stroke, rectangle, ellipse, pasted image, or cut/erase region, to select it.
- Drag the selected object to move it, or press `Delete` to remove it.
- Drag on empty screenshot space to select a rectangular image region.
- With a region selected, use `Cmd+C` to copy it, `Cmd+X` to cut it, and `Cmd+V` to paste it back into the canvas.
- Switching to another tool clears the rectangular area selection.

Select does not change the contents or shape of an existing annotation. To edit
existing text, press `T` for the Text tool and double-click the text; to renumber
a marker, press `F` and double-click the marker. Arrows,
pen strokes, rectangles, and ellipses can be moved or deleted, but not reshaped.
